questions.pregunta: Is the supply chain security program designed with, supported by, and implemented by an appropriate written review component? This is arequirement.

Yes, our supply chain security program is designed, supported, and implemented by the CTPAT-AEO internal and external audit procedure. In this procedure, we establish that we have a CTPAT-AEO Committee responsible for ensuring that all security processes described in the security program are carried out as designed.
Using the format 0001014899-EN - CTPAT-AEO Annual Security Audit Program, the members of the CTPAT/AEO Committee will be responsible for managing and executing this supply chain security audit program.This 0001014899-EN - CTPAT-AEO Annual Security Audit Program is reviewed, executed, and updated annually through the scheduling of the following audits conducted and administered by the CTPAT/AEO Security Committee.
Internal Audits:
The CTPAT/AEO Committee audits Corning Plants at least once a year, based on the guidelines outlined in the 0001014899-EN - CTPAT/AEO Annual Safety Audit Program, verifying that processes are executed in accordance with the CTPAT/AEO profiles and validating the corresponding evidence to ensure minimum compliance. Internal audits are cross-audits and are conducted among the member departments of the CTPAT/AEO Committee.
External audits:
External audits are conducted on business partners, and the CTPAT/AEO Safety Committee coordinates and executes them at least once a year, as outlined in the 0001015014-ES - Procedure for CTPAT and AEO Safety Reviews of Business Partners. 
For the implementation of the 0001014899-EN - CTPAT/AEO Annual Security Audit Program, the format 0001014900-ES - Internal and External Audit Questionnaire for CTPAT-AEO Compliance Assessment will be used.This questionnaire was developed based on the guidelines and requirements of the AEO standardsand the CTPAT Criteria.
As an alternative measure, a general internal and external audit is scheduled at least once a year,conducted by an independent external third party. This audit is intended to identify potential areasfor improvement and ensure the minimum compliance requirements indicated in the CTPAT/AEO programs.

The methodology to be used by the Security Committee for the risk analysis must be based on ISO 9000/9001 for its documentation control and on the corresponding security ISO standards (ISO 31000, ISO 31010, and ISO 28000) applicable to the company.
The COC Security Committee will use a risk analysis matrix, which will include instructions for completing it.
Field 1 of the Risk Analysis Matrix will list the sub standards and minimum-security criteria in accordance with the CTPAT and OEA guidelines.

Operational, Documentary, Terrorism, Contraband, Environmental, and Criminal.

The method for assessing, identifying, and controlling risks that could affect the continuity of COC operations will be based on the Risk Zone, which is the product of three factors: Probability, Impact, and Scope.
In the CTPAT-OEA risk analysis matrix are showing the risk assessments, the threat calification analysis, the monitoring and the control of the action plans.

questions.pregunta: If weaknesses are identified during business partners’ security assessments, are they addressed as soon as possible and are corrections implemented in a timely manner? Is it confirmed that deficiencies have been mitigated via documentary evidence? These are requirements.
questions.respuesta2025:
To determine whether a business partner meets CTPAT security criteria, we administer a questionnaire based on the minimum requirements of CTPAT and AEO and apply the following methodology.
1. Corning sends the questionnaire via email to the business partners.
2. The business partners review the questions and return the completed questionnaire.
3. Corning reviews the completed questionnaire and schedules a visit to validate the evidence.
4. Corning visits the business partner to validate the documentary evidence and conduct a physical inspection of their facilities.
5. The visit concludes, and both parties agree on action plans to address any findings.
6. Corning delivers an audit report with observations, comments, and recommendations.
7. Both parties follow up and monitor the agreed-upon action plans monthly until completion.
The next year, a CTPAT/AEO audit is conducted again.

Are written high security seal procedures in place that describe how seals are issued and controlled at the facility and during transit? event, communication protocols to partners, and investigation of the incident? Are the findings from the investigation documented, and any corrective actions implemented as quickly as possible? Do written seal controls include the following elements?
Controlling access to seals: management of seals is restricted to authorized personnel, secure storage, inventory, distribution, & tracking (seal log), recording the receipt of new seals, issuance of seals recorded in log, track seals via the log, and only trained, authorized personnel may affix seals to
instruments of international traffic (IIT).
Controlling seals in transit:
when picking up sealed IIT (or after stopping), verify the seal is intact with no signs of tampering, confirm the seal number matches what is noted on the shipping documents,
Seals broken in transit:
if load examined--record replacement seal number, the driver must immediately notify dispatch when a seal is broken, indicate who broke it, and provide the new seal number; the carrier must immediately notify the shipper, broker, and importer of the seal change, and the replacement seal number; and the shipper must note the replacement seal number in the seal log.
Seal discrepancies:
hold any seal discovered to be altered or tampered with to aid in the investigation, Investigate the discrepancy, follow-up with corrective measures (if warranted), and as applicable, report compromised seals to CBP and the appropriate foreign government to aid in the investigation. Procedure 0000003198-EN - Plant Safety Program, contemplates the following points:
4.2.19 Physical Security Tours.
4.2.19.1 Patrimonial Security in compliance with the C-TPAT / MX AEO, as a best practice it conducts documented physical security tours in the format 0000078768-EN in order to carry out an analysis to identify risks and weaknesses, in order to establish strategies that help mitigate risks
4.2.19.2 The Coordinator or the security officer makes the perimeter route and the internal coordinator randomly verifies that the route is carried out correctly.
a) .- The Security Officer or Coordinator carries with him the format 0000078768-EN where he notes findings and observations of the inspection carried out.
b) .- The Security Officer or Coordinator makes a tour of the entire perimeter of the plant to inspect meshes, concertinas, gates and turnstiles verifying that they are in good condition and functioning properly.
c) .- The Security Officer or Coordinator, makes a tour of the perimeter of the plant facilities to inspect doors, windows, shipping curtains and receipts verifying that they are in good condition and functioning properly.
d) .- At the end of the tour, the Security officer delivers the format 0000078768 to the Internal Coordinator.
e) .- The Internal Coordinator generates work orders, according to the findings found, supporting the Maintenance staff.
f) .- The Internal Coordinator records in 0000078768-EN format the order number assigned to the case.
g) .- If the findings are repetitive, the internal security coordinator informs the Security Supervisor.
h) .- The Security Supervisor is responsible for following up the findings.
i) .- If the finding has not had a solution, the Security supervisor will generate a corrective action with the quality department to solve the finding.

Yes, Corning CI-03155-DOC Identity and Access Management Standard, declares and protects the info with the next explanation,
7. STANDARD(S)
This section defines the requirements that are necessary to ensure effective identity and access control principles are applied. This section defines the requirements that are necessary to ensure effective implementation of information security awareness and training program at Corning.
USER ACCESS MANAGEMENT
7.1.1 User Identity [NIST CSF: PR.AC-1, PR.AC-4, PR.AC-6; NIST 800-171: 3.1.1, 3.1.5, 3.5.1; SOX: 2.7, 2.1; GDPR: Recital 30, Recital 57.2]
7.1.1.1 Each user (person, service, device, or other entity) accessing Corning Assets and information resources shall be issued a unique identity excluding generic accounts which are shared across users.
7.1.1.2 User identities and authorizations to key systems and resources shall be granted based on their role and job function requirements, while adhering to the principle of Least Privilege and Segregation of Duties.
7.1.1.3 Password protected user accounts shall be locked after a succession of 5 unsuccessful login attempts.
7.1.1.4 When a user forgets the password or gets the account lock out, the new password shall be obtained through the approved IT Service Desks Unlock or Password Reset process.
7.1.2 Provisioning and Access Management [NIST CSF: PR.AC-1, PR.IP-11; NIST 800-171: 3.1.4]
7.1.2.1 Account provisioning/de-provisioning requests or assignment of privileges shall go through a Corning-approved provisioning and/or ticketing system.
7.1.2.2 The request to create or grant access to these accounts shall be approved by an authorized Corning authority prior to pursuing the request and shall adhere to Segregation of Duties principle for the applicable systems.
7.1.2.3 Any override or exception to the Role-based access provisioning shall be approved by Corning Information Security and only for limited duration.
7.1.2.4 Non-privileged users shall be prevented from executing privileged functions. [NIST 800-171: 3.1.7]
7.1.3 User Authentication [NIST CSF: PR.AC-6; NIST 800-171: 3.5.2, 3.5.11; SOX: 2.7]
7.1.3.1 Users must be authenticated on each occasion before access is granted to a Corning system.
7.1.3.2 Authentication must occur against Cornings standard authentication system (e.g., Active Directory (AD)). Exceptions must be approved by the Corning Information Security team.
7.1.3.3 Users identity shall be verified before the user is allowed to reset their account password.
7.1.3.4 Authentication procedures shall obscure feedback (e.g., displaying asterisks in place of actual password characters or displaying actual characters for a very limited time before fully obscuring it), preventing unauthorized individuals from compromising authentication mechanisms.
7.1.4 Generic User Account Access Management
7.1.4.1 Generic accounts shall not be created unless it is explicitly approved by applicable authority as part of the exception process as mentioned in IT Acceptable Use Policy.
7.1.4.2 Generic accounts shall be used when creation of a named account is not possible i.e. when the shared resources exist in production or lab environments.
7.1.4.3 Generic accounts shall not be used by End Users to access Corning data.
7.1.4.4 Generic accounts shall be created in Active Directory and not locally on the system.
7.1.4.5 Generic accounts shall be assigned a designated owner who will be accountable for the use of the account and will provide approval for access. A primary and secondary owner shall be documented in a system of record and receive approval from respective Application/System Owner.
7.1.4.6 The designated owner shall be required to maintain account password and shall be the only person permitted to submit a request to change the password.
7.1.4.7 All users with access to generic accounts shall be documented, justified with a business reason, approved by the Application/System Owner and reviewed on a periodic basis.
7.1.4.8 Generic accounts shall not be enabled for the use of Instant Messaging (IM).
7.1.4.9 Account usage and distribution list shall be subject to a periodic review by Account Owner.
